title: Transplant status and rejection
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's transplant status or transplant complication only.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for lung transplant status.

HPI
Pt is a 73-year-old female presenting for routine outpatient follow-up regarding her double lung transplant performed 4 years ago. Pt reports feeling well overall and states she is doing well on her current immunosuppressant regimen. She denies any shortness of breath, chest pain, or significant fatigue. She notes no issues with medication side effects at this time. She is here for monitoring of transplant stability and maintenance of current medications.

Medication List
1. Tacrolimus 2mg BID
2. Mycophenolate mofetil 500mg BID
3. Prednisone 5mg daily

Review of Systems
Constitutional: No fever, chills, or weight changes.
Respiratory: No cough, dyspnea, or wheezing.
Cardiovascular: No palpitations or edema.
Gastrointestinal: No nausea or diarrhea.
Neurological: No tremors or headaches.
Musculoskeletal: No joint pain.
All other systems reviewed and negative.

Social History
Pt lives at home with her spouse. Retired. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol use.

Family History
Mother: Hypertension.
Father: Type 2 Diabetes.
Siblings: Healthy.

Vitals
BP: 128/78
HR: 72 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 98% on RA
Ht: 5'4"
Wt: 145 lbs

Recent Labs
WBC: 5.2
Hgb: 12.1
Plt: 150k
Creatinine: 1.0
eGFR: 82
Tacrolimus trough level: 8.5 ng/mL

Exam
General: Alert, oriented x3, in no acute distress.
Respiratory: CTAB. Breath sounds clear bilaterally. No adventitious sounds.
Cardiovascular: RRR, S1, S2 noted. No murmurs.
Skin: No rashes or lesions.
Extremities: No edema.

Assessment
1. Status post double lung transplant (4 years ago). Pt is stable on current immunosuppression. No signs of transplant complication.

Plan
1. Continue current immunosuppressant medications as prescribed.
2. Continue monitoring tacrolimus trough levels.
3. Routine f/u in 3 months.

Electronically signed, T. Haddad, NP, 05/14/2026
